result:
Solution 1's answer of 6 matches what I recall of the literature on this problem. I did not derive the upper bound myself, and I did not re-check every step of Solution 1's proof.

A quadratic rational map has Aut(f) trivial, Z/2, or S₃, so the nonabelian case is Aut(f) ≅ S₃. Such maps are twists of z ↦ 1/z², and the three fixed-point multipliers are all −2.

Solution 1 gives an explicit map with three rational fixed points 0, 1, 2. It also finds three rational preimages of those fixed points, namely 4/3, ∞ and 2/3, for 6 rational preperiodic points in total. I did not check that this map has S₃ automorphism group or that its fixed-point multipliers are −2. The claim that no further rational preperiodic points exist rests on discriminant computations that I did not verify.

Solution 2 claims 12 by counting S₃-orbits of rational points. That count does not follow, because a size-6 orbit of period-3 points and other extra orbits are not shown to exist for any such map. I recall the true maximum being smaller.

Solution 3 claims 4, but Solution 1's example already exceeds that, so 4 is not the maximum.

CHOICE: 1
